newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up on Wednesday due to heavy overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at 19,540 yuan ($2,354) per tonne, rising 110 yuan. It opened at 19,690 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 19,700 and a low of 19,530.
November rose 90 to 19,040, December 30 to 19,230, January 100 to 19,520, March 100 to 19,540, April 140 to 19,540 and May 140 to 19,600.
Combined volume doubled to 61,620 yuan from 30,730.
Copper opened higher sharply but profit-taking and fresh selling pushed the contracts down steadily from highs but still up from Tuesday's close.
"Many investors took advantage of LME gains to liquidate their long positions at high levels and then stay on the sidelines," one trader said.
"They did not want to hold long positions at the current high levels, on concerns about poor fundamentals," he added.
"But LME gains encouraged them to build many short positions," a second trader said.
"Investors were mixed about later trends," a third trader said. "Copper will rise further if most contracts remain above the 19,500-yuan level, otherwise it will fall again."
Analysts expect copper to move around 19,500 in the absence of market-moving news in the next few days.
Aluminium ended unchanged. The only traded November contract ended unchanged at 13,450 yuan per tonne, with volume of 390 tonnes.
